title: Road Test Guide
summary: What to bring, what the examiner checks, and the mistakes that fail most drivers.

blocks.text: Requirements differ by state, so confirm them on your state agency's website: how long you must hold your permit, any supervised practice hours, whether you need an appointment, and which documents to bring.

items: Practice in the kind of traffic you will see on the test: residential streets, intersections with signals and stop signs, and lane changes.
Practice the maneuvers your state tests, such as parallel parking, backing in a straight line, turning around in a narrow street, and parking on a hill.
Drive the car you will test in, so its size, mirrors and controls feel familiar.

blocks.text: Most examiners check the vehicle before you drive. If something required is not working, the test may be cancelled.

items: Current registration and proof of insurance or financial responsibility, as your state requires.
Working headlights, brake lights, turn signals, horn and emergency flashers.
Seat belts that work, safe tires, and a windshield that does not block your view.
Mirrors positioned so you can see behind and to the sides.

blocks.text: The examiner may ask you to show where controls are: wipers, defroster, headlights and high beams, hazard lights, horn and parking brake. Know them before you arrive.

items: Adjust your seat, head restraint and mirrors before you start the engine.
Fasten your seat belt and make sure your passenger has fastened theirs.
Check your mirrors and look over your shoulder before pulling away from the curb.
Signal, then move into traffic only when there is a safe gap.

rows: Check mirrors often and look over your shoulder before changing lanes, merging or pulling out.
Come to a complete stop behind the stop line or crosswalk; do not roll through.
Stay at or below the limit and adjust for conditions; driving too slowly can also cost points.
Keep a safe following distance and leave room to the side.
Signal early, slow before the turn, and finish in the correct lane.
Yield to pedestrians and to traffic that has the right-of-way.
Smooth steering and braking, both hands on the wheel, and the car kept in its lane.

blocks.text: Turn your head when you check mirrors and blind spots. Examiners can only score the checks they can see.

items: Rolling stops at stop signs or before turning right on red.
Not checking the blind spot before changing lanes or pulling away from the curb.
Speeding, including in school zones and work zones.
Failing to yield to pedestrians or oncoming traffic.
Wide or cut-short turns, or ending a turn in the wrong lane.
Hitting or climbing the curb while parking.
Forgetting to signal, or signaling too late.

blocks.text: Dangerous actions usually end the test immediately, for example running a red light, causing the examiner to step in or brake, or a collision.

items: Arrive early with your permit, documents and appointment details.
Listen carefully. If you do not understand an instruction, ask the examiner to repeat it.
If you make a small mistake, stay calm and keep driving safely. One error rarely fails the whole test.
Drive the way you practiced: smooth, legal and predictable.

keyPoints: Check your state's requirements and bring the right documents.
Make sure the car's lights, signals, horn, brakes and belts all work.
Make full stops behind the stop line, every time.
Turn your head to check mirrors and blind spots so the examiner sees it.
Signal early, keep a safe gap, and yield to pedestrians.
Stay calm. One small mistake is rarely the end of the test.
